title: Model rollout tranche scheduler and KV stress heuristics
body:
Purpose:
- Quick operational workbook to schedule multi-region model rollouts in staggered tranches and estimate the KV cache footprint, transient pressure, and GPU slot impact across regions. Intended as a lightweight, editable sheet used by infra on-call + launch PMs.

Key goals:
- Produce conservative peak and steady-state KV GB estimates per region for each tranche.
- Translate KV pressure into GPU slot headroom requirements (safety factor included).
- Provide simple heuristics for tranche sizing and warmup cadence to avoid cross-region eviction storms.

Assumptions (editable):
- model_variant: "LARGE-REDWOOD-7B" baseline; quantized variant expected to reduce kv_per_request by 12% but increase CPU overhead.
- tokenization: avg_tokens_per_request = 220 (median 180, p95 490)
- kv_entry_size_avg = 2.2 KB (includes key, metadata, TTL overhead)
- kv_hit_rate warmup assumptions: 0% pre-warm, 20% after seeded warmup, 60% after steady-state warmup + prefix caching.
- GPU slot throughput (baseline): 220 qps per slot for this model at target latency with continuous batching; burstable to 350 for short periods.
- safety_margin_slots = 1.25 (25% headroom)

Definitions / heuristics used:
- kv_per_request = (avg_context_tokens / kv_entry_tokens_covered) * kv_entry_size_avg; kv_entry_tokens_covered ~ 128 tokens per KV entry typically.
- kv_footprint_gb = (daily_unique_kv_keys_active * kv_entry_size_avg) / (1024^3) * regional_multiplier
- regional_multiplier: accounts for hot-shards and replication (1.0 for single-zone local, 1.15 for multi-AZ, 1.35 for cross-region caching replicas)

Scenario table (editable rows):
- Columns: tranche_id | start_date | region | target_weekly_rps | ramp_weeks | avg_ctx_len | kv_hit_rate_post_warm | estimated_daily_unique_keys | kv_footprint_gb | gpu_slots_est_peak | gpu_slots_est_steady | recommended_warmup_action

Rows (examples):
1 | 2026-03-10 | us-west1 | 18,000 | 3 | 220 | 0.2 | 120,000 | 0.25 GB | 90 slots | 45 slots | seeded-shadow-traffic 24h -> 7d
2 | 2026-03-24 | eu-west1 | 9,000 | 2 | 220 | 0.15 | 70,000 | 0.14 GB | 45 slots | 23 slots | seeded-shadow + prefetch prefixes
3 | 2026-04-07 | ap-south1 | 6,000 | 4 | 260 | 0.12 | 65,000 | 0.14 GB | 30 slots | 18 slots | extended-warmup 10d (low cadence)
4 | 2026-04-21 | us-east1 | 25,000 | 3 | 200 | 0.22 | 175,000 | 0.36 GB | 125 slots | 62 slots | split-tranche A/B, holdback 15%

Calculation notes (how numbers produced):
- estimated_qps_to_slots (peak) = ceil((target_weekly_rps / 7 / 24 / 3600 * 3600) / per_slot_qps_peak) -> simplified to target_rps_peak / per_slot_qps_peak; we assume 10% short-term burst factor on top of target_rps to size peak.
- gpu_slots_est_peak uses per_slot_qps_peak = 350 qps (burst) then applies safety_margin_slots, round up to integer.
- gpu_slots_est_steady uses sustained per_slot_qps = 220 qps, includes 25% safety margin.
- estimated_daily_unique_keys derived from projected unique users * average sessions * prefix churn factor; default prefix churn 0.37 for chat-like workloads.
- kv_footprint_gb = (estimated_daily_unique_keys * kv_entry_size_avg) / 1,073,741,824 * regional_multiplier

Risk matrix (top concerns):
- Rapid simultaneous tranches across small regions causing KV eviction cascades -> Mitigation: enforce global stagger window and soft admission quotas per region.
- Underestimated kv_entry_size due to richer metadata -> Mitigation: run sampling job on shadow traffic to empirically measure entry size before tranche.
- Unexpected high context lengths from a few power users -> Mitigation: per-customer token caps and dynamic batching policies; increase KV TTL eviction aggressiveness for new model for first 48h.

Operational heuristics (practical rules):
- Tranche cadence: avoid scheduling tranches in the same major region family (US/EU/AP) within 7 days of each other unless pre-warmed to >=40% kv_hit_rate.
- Warmup sequence: 24h seeded shadow (10% traffic), 72h progressive ramp (30-60%), then can open full traffic.
- Prefetch policy: precompute top-10 prefixes for heavy customers and push to regional KV for the first 72h.
- Autoscale guards: set 'soft admission' throttle at 85% of sustained slot capacity to trigger auto-fallback to quantized variant.

Suggested quick experiments to improve confidence before tranche 1:
- Sample-run: replay 48h of production traces against model-variant offline to measure kv_key churn and median kv_entry_size. (ticket JIRA-INF-8421)
- Shadow prefetch A/B test: prefetch top prefixes for subset of users and observe kv_hit_rate uplift and eviction delta over 72h.
- Cold-start stress: schedule a 2h synthetic surge at midnight local to measure eviction latency and cross-AZ replication load.

Action items (owners):
- Aisha: run entry-size samplers and produce summary by 2026-02-22.
- Marc: prepare tranche gating playbook and add soft admission throttles in infra config by 2026-03-01.
- Wei: run regional shadow-replay (eu/us/ap) and return kv_churn metrics by 2026-02-28.
- Sofia: coordinate with product launch PM to pin tranche dates and holdback fractions.

Notes / free-form observations:
- Early checks indicate per-request KV bytes dominated by metadata fields; trimming or compressing metadata yields largest marginal reduction in footprint.
- For small regions (ap-south1) prioritize extended ramp over immediate slot allocation to avoid wasting reserved GPUs during slow warmups.

Open questions (to resolve in next review):
- Should replication topology for KV be relaxed for this model for first 72h to conserve cluster memory? (tradeoff: higher cross-region latency on misses)
- Is 25% safety_margin_slots sufficient for simultaneous 10% burst across 3 regions?

Appendix: quick formulas (for copy-paste)
- kv_footprint_gb = (daily_unique_keys * kv_entry_size_bytes) / 1,073,741,824 * regional_multiplier
- slots_needed_peak = ceil((target_peak_rps * 1.10) / per_slot_qps_peak * safety_margin_slots)
- slots_needed_steady = ceil((target_steady_rps) / per_slot_qps_steady * safety_margin_slots)

Version history:
- 2026-02-15 A.Patel initial draft with sample scenarios
- 2026-02-22 Wei Z. ran sample-replay and updated churn assumptions
- 2026-03-03 Marc O'Neill updated warmup heuristics and added action owners

End of sheet.
